To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the area of the cortex relative to the whole bone area is a useful index of bone density and that the index is significantly correlated with the mineral content of human bones.

the cortical bone of the human finger is an excellent model of bone for the study of osteoporosis, because it has the advantages of being easy to study and of having a high degree of correlation between the mineral content and the thickness of the cortical layer.
the area ratio of the cortex to the area of rest of the finger bone correlates highly significantly with the actual mineral density of finger bone, as assessed by burning the bone to ash.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an objective index for the assessment of osteoporosis of finger bones.
the use of X-ray images of bones to estimate the mineral content of the bone.
the use of X-ray images of finger bones as a method of assessing osteoporosis, and with the use of this method to study the effects of ovariectomy on the bones of female rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a causal relationship between osteoarthritis and osteoporosis in the finger joints.
there is a strong correlation between bone mineral content and cortical thickness in human finger bones.
the area ratio of the cortical layer to the total bone area is a useful index of demin eralisation of finger bones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a high correlation between the mineral content of the finger bones and the area ratio is a strong argument for the use of the finger bone as an indicator of the general mineral content of the skeleton.

the cortical thickness of the finger bones is a useful index of the mineral content of the finger bones and is a sensitive index of the demineralisation which occurs in the osteoporosis associated with aging.
the ratio of the area occupied by the cortical layer to the area of bone in the X-ray image is a useful measure of the degree of demineralization of the finger bones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cortical area ratio is a useful index of the demineralisation of human finger bones.
the cortical layer of the finger bones can be used as an index of bone demineralisation.
it is important to be aware that the bone mineral density (BMD) of the hand is different from the BMD of the hip and spine.
